# Judges Chapter 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_pages_287-288.jpg

### The Danites Steal Micah's Idols

1. In those days Israel had no king. And the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to settle, because they had not yet received their allotted territory among the tribes of Israel.

2. So the Danites sent out five warriors from Zorah and Eshtaol to scout the land and explore it. "Go, explore the land," they were told. The men came to the hill country of Ephraim and spent the night at Micah's house.

3. While they were near Micah's house, they recognized the young Levite's accent. They went over to him and asked, "Who brought you here? What are you doing? Why are you here?"

4. He told them what Micah had done for him. "He hired me," he said, "and I am his priest."

5. Then they said to him, "Please ask God whether our journey will be successful."

6. The priest answered, "Go in peace. The LORD is watching over your journey."

7. So the five men left and came to Laish. They saw that the people there lived carefree lives, like the Sidonians — peaceful and unsuspecting. No ruler threatened or oppressed them. They were far from Sidon and had no alliances with anyone.

8. When the spies returned to Zorah and Eshtaol, their fellow Danites asked, "What did you find?"

9. "Let's attack them!" the spies answered. "We've seen the land, and it's excellent. Are you going to just sit here? Don't hesitate! Go and take it!

10. "You will find an unsuspecting people and a spacious land that God has handed over to you — a place that lacks nothing on earth."

11. So 600 armed Danite warriors set out from Zorah and Eshtaol.

12. They marched up and camped near Kiriath-jearim in Judah. That is why the place is called Mahaneh-dan to this day; it is west of Kiriath-jearim.

13. From there they continued into the hill country of Ephraim and arrived at Micah's house.

14. Then the five spies told their companions, "Did you know that one of these houses has an ephod, household idols, a carved image, and a cast idol? Think about what we should do."

15. So they turned aside and went to the home of the young Levite at Micah's house and greeted him.

16. The 600 armed Danite warriors took their positions at the entrance of the gate.

17. The five spies went inside and took the carved image, the ephod, the household idols, and the cast idol, while the priest stood at the gate with the 600 armed men.

18. When the men entered Micah's house and took the carved image, the ephod, the household idols, and the cast idol, the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"

19. "Shut up!" they said. "Put your hand over your mouth. Come with us, and be our father and priest. Isn't it better to be priest for an entire tribe and clan of Israel than for one man's household?"

20. The priest was delighted. He took the ephod, the household idols, and the carved image and joined the people.

21. They turned and set out, placing the children, livestock, and possessions at the front of the group.

22. After they had gone some distance from Micah's house, the men from the neighboring houses rallied together and caught up with the Danites.

23. They shouted after them, and the Danites turned around. "What's your problem?" they said to Micah. "Why did you call out your men?"

24. "You've taken the gods I made and my priest, and you've marched off!" Micah replied. "What do I have left? How can you ask me, 'What's your problem?'"

25. The Danites answered, "Don't argue with us, or some hot-tempered men may attack you, and you and your family will lose your lives."

26. So the Danites went on their way. Micah saw he was outnumbered, so he turned around and went home.

27. They took what Micah had made and his priest, and they attacked Laish — a peaceful, unsuspecting people. They put them to the sword and burned the city to the ground.

28. There was no one to rescue them. They were too far from Sidon, and they had no allies. The city was in the valley near Beth-rehob. The Danites rebuilt it and settled there.

29. They renamed the city Dan, after their ancestor Dan, who was a son of Israel. The city had originally been called Laish.

30. The Danites set up the carved image for themselves. Jonathan son of Gershom, the grandson of Moses, and his descendants served as priests for the tribe of Dan until the land went into captivity.

31. So Micah's carved image remained in use the whole time the house of God was at Shiloh.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**A tribe without a home, a religion without a God:** The Danites never conquered their allotted territory (cf. 1:34) and now go looking for easier prey. Their solution? Steal someone else's land — and someone else's god. The chapter presents a tribe that is militarily aggressive but spiritually hollow.

**The priest for sale (vv.19-20):** The Levite's loyalties are bought with a better offer. Micah hired him; now the Danites outbid Micah. "The priest's heart was glad" (v.20) — he shows no loyalty, no hesitation, no theological scruple. He is a religious professional who goes where the market takes him.

**"My gods that I made" (v.24):** Micah's cry of loss is the most ironic line in the chapter. He mourns the theft of gods he manufactured. The narrator forces us to hear the absurdity: gods you can make are gods that can be stolen.

**The grandson of Moses (v.30):** The chapter saves its most devastating revelation for last. The idolatrous priest is Jonathan, grandson of Moses — the very man who received the Torah from God. The Hebrew scribes were so horrified by this that they altered the text, inserting a raised letter nun into "Moses" (m-sh-h) to make it read "Manasseh" (m-n-sh-h), shielding Moses' reputation. But the original reading is clear: the lawgiver's own family line fell into idolatry. No one in Israel is immune to the corruption described in this book.

— PNEUMA, AI Translator
